labels.description: The new-product sales share rolls forward from approximately 25% of 2024 sales to approximately 25% of 2025 sales, with the percentage and all other text unchanged.
labels.rationale: Minor: the only change is a fiscal-year roll-forward (2024 to 2025) with the 25% figure unchanged.

labels.description: The foreign sales mix rolls forward from fiscal 2024 to fiscal 2025 with identical percentages (43% outside the U.S., 23% Europe, 5% Western Hemisphere, 15% Asia-Pacific and Africa), the stale parenthetical dating Egypt's highly inflationary treatment to the fiscal fourth quarter of 2024 is dropped while Egypt stays on the list, and the subheading label changes from Anti-bribery to Anti-corruption with the same FCPA and U.K. Bribery Act content.
labels.rationale: Minor: every change is a fiscal-year roll-forward, removal of an outdated date qualifier with no change in the listed countries, or a relabeled subheading with no change in substance.

labels.description: Russia is dropped as the named jurisdiction for patent exploitation and sales restrictions, the named tariff targets China, Mexico and Canada are dropped while tariffs move from recently announced to has imposed and/or announced, data localization laws and data transfer restrictions are added as protective policies, and rising is removed from conflict in the Middle East.
labels.rationale: Criterion 2: named jurisdictions (Russia, China, Mexico, Canada) are dropped, and criteria 1 and 3 also apply because a new exposure (data localization and transfer restrictions) is added and tariffs move from announced to imposed.

labels.description: Increasing use of and reliance on third parties is added as a driver of cybersecurity risk, and the AI risk driver is widened from AI alone to AI and other emerging technology.
labels.rationale: Criterion 1: a new dependency (reliance on third parties) is disclosed as increasing attack exposure, and criterion 3 applies because the scope of the technology risk widens to other emerging technology.

labels.description: The Orthopaedics separation announced in October 2025, targeted for completion 18 to 24 months after announcement, may be delayed or not completed on the contemplated terms because it depends on works council consultations, final Board approval and regulatory approvals.

The planned Orthopaedics separation will involve significant costs, and the Company may not achieve its expected strategic and financial benefits because they rest on assumptions that may prove incorrect.
The Company cannot predict the separation's effect on its common stock price, which may fall below its pre-separation value and be more volatile around the time of the separation.
